subject.title: Telegram: support fail-closed unknown-group handling with optional auto-leave

question: Should Telegram add an opt-in unknown-group action (`ignore`/`warn`/`leave`), and what exact boundary should allow auto-leave to fire?
rationale: The source-reproducible gap is real, but the fix adds new config and a destructive Telegram side effect in an authorization path, so automation should not choose the product/security semantics alone.

options.title: Approve narrow opt-in action
options.body: Add optional Telegram-only unknown-group handling that defaults to current drop behavior and fires only for the chat-not-allowlisted decision, with cooldown, docs, tests, and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Fold into broader group pairing/audit design
options.body: Keep this issue linked while maintainers design the wider group approval, owner notification, and audit posture tracked by related group-security issues.

options.title: Keep deny-only behavior
options.body: Decline warn/leave behavior for now and document BotFather group-join controls plus current allowlist/logging behavior as the supported posture.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow opt-in action
recommendation.body: Add optional Telegram-only unknown-group handling that defaults to current drop behavior and fires only for the chat-not-allowlisted decision, with cooldown, docs, tests, and live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame/log places the active Telegram group-policy and runtime surfaces in Peter Steinberger's recent history.
